messages:
marta (support): Hi team — customer reported a huge bulk embeddings job started hitting 429s mid-run. They say it was steady for ~20m then we started returning 429s and some errors showing 'rate limit exceeded' and 'batch dimension mismatch' in their app logs. They gave a request_id: rq_9Xl3a and sample cURL.  They need a repro and a quick mitigation. :eyes:

sandeep (infra-oncall): Thanks — can you paste the raw headers (response headers) and the exact curl they used?  primary suspect is burst throttling + concurrent workers.  Also: what model and batch_size?

marta (support): Paste from customer: ```curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings
 -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>"
 -H "Content-Type: application/json"
 -d '{"model":"text-embed-compact-v1","inputs":["...large array omitted..."]}' ```
They used batch_size ~ 5000 (they send arrays of 5k small strings), model is text-embed-compact-v1 according to them. Response headers snippet they pasted: ```HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
X-RateLimit-Limit: 60000
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-RateLimit-Reset: 1678900
Retry-After: 2
```
They also logged an error in the app: "embedding dimension mismatch: expected 384 got 1536" — not sure if it's the same job or a downstream consumer mismatch.

sandeep (infra-oncall): Ok a few things: 1) X-RateLimit-Limit/Remaining look like per-minute token-ish counters (we have burst windows). If Remaining hits 0 we will 429 until reset. 2) Retry-After: 2 means short window but if they immediately retry with many concurrent workers they'll overshoot the global concurrency and keep getting 429s. 3) For huge fanout/batch patterns we recommend chunking to <1024 items or throttling concurrency to <= 8 parallel requests.

sandeep (infra-oncall): Quick mitigation we can suggest to customer: exponential backoff with jitter + reduce batch size. Example pseudo: ```python
backoff = 0.5
for attempt in range(6):
    try: send_request()
    except HTTP429:
        sleep(backoff + random()*backoff)
        backoff *= 2
```
Also ask them to set max concurrency and add per-worker random jitter.

marta (support): Noted. Customer says they have multiple worker pods (K8s) all firing at once; they were doing one big job as a bulk pipeline. They're worried about losing work if we force them too small. They asked if we can temporarily raise allowance or give a burst window.

olivia (billing): If this is a customer hitting hosted limits we can fast-track a temporary quota bump for a known run — need org id and approximate token counts. But we should only do this if it's not a misconfigured client (dimension mismatch). Also remind them quota increases are tracked and may require committed capacity for long term.

tom (ml-eng): On the dimension mismatch: two possibilities: 1) They're calling the embeddings endpoint with a model that outputs 1536-d vectors but their downstream index expects 384-d (or vice versa). 2) They might be mixing models in the pipeline (some records embedded with compact-v1(384) and others with standard-v2(1536)). Ask them to check model names in their ingestion.

tom (ml-eng): Repro steps to validate quickly: 1) Run a single small request and inspect vector length: ```curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' -d '{"model":"text-embed-compact-v1","input":"test"}' | jq '.data[0].embedding | length'```
If the length is 384 but their index expects 1536, that's the mismatch. If length varies between requests, they are likely switching models or using an older client.

sandeep (infra-oncall): For the 429s, we should also check whether this customer was routed through our regional rate limiter or global. Marta can you grab the routing headers (X-Route-Region / X-Plan-Tier) from their next failing request? If it's global (us-west), they might be hitting a shared burst cap.

marta (support): I asked customer to run the single-request check and to send back X-headers from a failing request. They ran it and returned: ```X-Route-Region: us-east-1
X-Plan-Tier: developer
X-RateLimit-Limit: 30000
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
Retry-After: 1```
Customer attached their ingestion logs and it shows many workers retrying immediately on 429s (no jitter).

sandeep (infra-oncall): That's consistent. Plan is developer (shared). We need to advise both short-term and long-term: short-term -> reduce concurrent requests, add backoff + jitter; if they need big throughput for one-off job we can escalate to temporary dedicated burst (ops-assisted) if they provide org id and expected tokens. Long-term -> Dedicated or reserved capacity.

olivia (billing): I'll prepare an ops-assisted trial for one-off runs (we do a soft lift of burst caps) — need org id + scheduled window. Note: if they want sustained lift we'll propose Dedicated.

marta (support): Customer also reported some 'dimension mismatch' logs for a subset of items. They confirmed they were using two different service accounts (one running old client that defaults to text-embed-v1, another using compact). So tom's theory holds. I told them to standardize model and reindex.

tom (ml-eng): Good. For them to reindex without downtime they can do side-by-side indexing with a version flag and bulk swap. Also, add an assertion in their ingestion pipeline to check vector length and drop/alert on mismatches. Example check: ```if len(vec) != expected_dim: raise ValueError(f"dim mismatch {len(vec)} != {expected_dim}")```

marta (support): Action items for support: 1) Send the user back a short playbook (reduce batch_size to <=1024, limit concurrency, add exponential backoff w/ jitter, check model names and client versions, run the single-request vector-length check). 2) Offer temporary ops-assisted burst if they provide org id and job schedule. 3) If they want sustained throughput, route to sales for Dedicated.

sandeep (infra-oncall): I'll also flag their request_id rq_9Xl3a in infra logs and confirm whether their traffic hit a per-region burst gate. If we find an infra bug (e.g., overly aggressive windowing) we'll escalate.

rate-limiter-bot: Alert: per-minute token bucket for region us-east-1 reached 0 for tenant developer-tier during 1990012300-1990012360. Auto-throttle engaged.

marta (support): I'll send the playbook and ask for org id + expected tokens. I'll also include the curl vector-length snippet and the pseudo backoff code. Thanks all — followups once customer confirms. :thumbsup:
